name: Datu houses and the torogan
description: Precolonial datu lived in the largest houses of the barangay: raised on thick posts, with steep thatched roofs. Visayan chiefs' houses were noted by Spanish writers for their size and the number of their posts, and a datu's house was where disputes were heard and guests received. Among the Maranao of Lake Lanao, the torogan is the ancestral house of a sultan or datu, raised on large round posts, with an upswept roof and carved, flared beam ends (panolong) decorated with okir. In this game the Bahay ng Datu borrows these forms; the Maranao look is torogan-inspired, not a copy of any standing house.
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
Rodrigo D. Perez III, Rosario S. Encarnacion and Julian E. Dacanay Jr., Folk Architecture (GCF Books, 1989)
